# GAS Lab Wiki v2 — Index & Ingestion Manifest

v2 (2026-06-03) supersedes v1.0 (2026-05-19). It folds in field-research answers to the questions that pestered v1 (see `questions.md`) and restructures the document as **self-contained chunk files** designed for both human navigation and knowledge-graph / RAG ingestion. When this wiki contradicts older notes, this wiki wins for GASLab purposes.

> **Scope change (2026-06-03):** the operating envelope was narrowed from 1990–2020 to **petrol 1990–2010 (Euro 1–5)**. Chemistry tied to the post-2010 "modern" vehicle set (Euro 6/7, the 2010–2020 Era-3 fault patterns) is **out of scope** and is not carried into v2. GDI and early-turbo failure modes remain in scope only where the vehicles were sold within 1990–2010.
## How v2 differs from v1

The reasoning grammar and every numeric threshold are preserved. The `ChemicalSignature` contract is now **34-value** (v2.1 timing-taxonomy revision retired `WRONG_VALVE_TIMING` for three `CAM_TIMING_*` states — see GASWIKI-06B and GAS_VOCABULARY §21). v2 adds:
- **Brettschneider reliability model** — λ is a measure of the *sample*, not the *engine*; per-fault reliability and an explicit uncertainty band (research q1, q2).
- **Pre-cat leak vs sample-handling-error** resolution via OBD fuel-trim correlation and the probe-occlusion test (research q3).
- **ECU-vs-tailpipe divergence magnitudes** quantified per fault, feeding the truth-vs-perception detector (research q6).

- **Five oil-burn failure modes** (worn rings, valve-stem seals, stuck-open PCV, head-gasket oil breach, turbo turbine-seal leak) mapped onto existing enum values with RPM-delta sub-modes (research q4).
- **Dual-idle (idle vs 2500 RPM) catalyst test** distinguishing weak/lazy from dead/poisoned converters (research q10).
- **Timing-fault RPM-differential separation matrix** and Speed-Density-vs-MAF rich/lean behaviour (research q7).
- **Fuel-formulation (E5/E10) and altitude** shifts and why the triangle gate must *not* be relaxed (research q9).

- **Proposed v2.x enum additions** appendix — new oil-burn cases recorded for a future contract revision, still mapped onto existing values (distinct from the v2.1 cam-timing change, which does alter the contract surface).

OBD-II depth from research q7 (DTC tables, Mode `$06` MID/TID, freeze-frame, in-cylinder pressure) is summarised as **OBDLab / DTCLab territory** with cross-references, not reproduced in full — GASLab's emit boundary is tailpipe 5-gas only.

1. **Front-matter** (YAML) on every file carries: `chunk_id`, `title`, `summary`, `entities_defined`, `related_chunks`, `sources`. KG ingestion should treat `entities_defined` as the node list this chunk is authoritative for.

2. **Stable anchor IDs.** Every fault entity, rule, gate, and test has an explicit anchor of the form `{#FAULT_<NAME>}`, `{#RULE_<NAME>}`, `{#GATE_<NAME>}`, `{#TEST_<NAME>}`, `{#CONCEPT_<NAME>}`. Cross-references use these IDs (e.g. `→ RULE_MASKING`) rather than fragile section numbers. Legacy `§n.n` numbers are retained in parentheses for traceability to v1.

3. **Typed fault-entity records.** Each fault in the atlas (chunks 05, 06A, 06B) uses the same key list so relations extract uniformly: `chemical_state`, `dna_gate`, `match_class`, `gas_vector`, `discriminator`, `rpm_delta`, `related`, `sources`.
4. **One concept per section.** Sections are never split across chunks; cross-chunk links are expected and resolvable by `chunk_id` + anchor.
5. **Provenance.** Content new in v2 is tagged inline `[v2: qN]` so the graph can attribute each claim to its research source.

# 1. Role, Boundaries & DNA-Gated Ingestion
## 1.1 Role and boundaries {#CONCEPT_ROLE}
GASLab is one of four leaves of the 4DLab fan-in. It converts a technician-entered 5-gas reading plus a slim DNA slice into one canonical `chemical_state`.
technician-entered 5-gas reading ─┤

**Operating envelope.** Petrol vehicles 1990–2010 (Euro 1 – Euro 5); manually-entered analyser readings (no live CAN streaming); 5-gas analysers only (no 4-gas fallback — NOₓ channel required); warm-engine samples only (cold open-loop is rejected, see → CONCEPT_RPM_BUCKET in GASWIKI-02). Post-2010 "modern" chemistry (Euro 6/7, 2010–2020 patterns) is out of scope.
## 1.2 What GASLab sees {#CONCEPT_GASLAB_INPUTS}
| NOₓ (ppm) | technician form | electrochemical; 5-gas only — required |
## 1.3 What GASLab emits — GasLabPayload {#CONCEPT_GASLABPAYLOAD}
The contract surface, governed by `SEMANTIC_CONTRACT.md` §4.4 (with the v1.1 widening that put all five measured gases on the wire):
"chemical_state": "RICH_MIXTURE",       // 34-value enum, see GAS_VOCABULARY §3
"gas_co": 4.5,                          // vol %
"gas_hc": 650,                          // ppm
"gas_co2": 9.5,                         // vol %
"gas_nox": 15,                          // ppm
"lambda_chem": 0.82,                    // Brettschneider
"lambda_measured": 1.02,                // optional directly-measured analyser λ (no-OBD path)
"sample_validity": "VALID"              // VALID | BORDERLINE | INVALID | EXTERNAL_O2_SUSPECT

The contract widening (`gas_co2`, `gas_nox`) requires a matching update to `COMLab/comlab/schemas/ingestion.py::GasLabPayload` and to `SEMANTIC_CONTRACT.md` itself before GASLab is wired to COMLab — see `GAS_VOCABULARY.md` §12.1.
GASLab returns **exactly one** `chemical_state`; ambiguity is collapsed by rule priority (→ GASWIKI-04 named overrides).
## 1.4 The GasLabDnaView — the slim DNA slice {#CONCEPT_GASLABDNAVIEW}
| `cylinder_count` | `vin_dna.cylinder_count` | per-cylinder misfire math (`ΔO₂ ≈ 21 / N`) |
| `emissions.upstream_o2_type` | `vin_dna.emissions.upstream_o2_type` | calibrates sensor-bias signatures |
| `emissions.has_catalyst` (from `downstream_o2_present`) | `vin_dna.emissions.downstream_o2_present` | switches "with cat" / "no cat" threshold tables |
| `target_lambda_v112` | `vin_dna.target_lambda_v112` | per-vehicle CoC empirical target |
| `fuel_type` *(proposed v2)* | `vin_dna.fuel_type` | E5/E10/winter-blend correction context `[v2: q9]` |
| `altitude_band` *(proposed v2)* | session/context | informational only — λ math is altitude-invariant `[v2: q9]` |
| `confidence` | `vin_dna.confidence` | gates limited-scope fallback (→ GASWIKI-10) |

Code-side type lives in `gaslab/dna_view.py` (`GasLabDnaView`); the composition's `_build_gas_dna_view` builds it. The two proposed v2 fields (`fuel_type`, `altitude_band`) are context-only — see GASWIKI-02 §2.8 for why neither relaxes any gate.
## 1.5 DNA-gated ingestion model {#CONCEPT_DNA_GATED_INGESTION}

**Consequence for GASLab.** GASLab does **not** maintain its own per-vehicle physical-bound table. It assumes incoming readings sit within the analyser measurement envelope (HC 0–20 000 ppm, CO 0–15 %, CO₂ 0–22 %, O₂ 0–22 %, NOₓ 0–5 000 ppm). What GASLab still owns:
- **chemistry-level validity gates** — the Exhaust Gas Triangle and dilution screen (→ GATE_TRIANGLE, GATE_DILUTION in GASWIKI-04). These are physics, not vehicle-specific.
- **internal sanity rails** — values that pass the UI bound but are chemically impossible (e.g. CO > 12 % at idle with valid CO₂) raise `SAMPLE_INVALID`.

**What it replaces.** The old static `physical_sensor_bounds.json` pattern (no DNA awareness) is gone; the blindspot it caused (e.g. RPM allowed 0–8000 regardless of redline) is resolved at the UI before any value reaches GASLab.

**Tradeoff.** The UI must call DNALab synchronously before the technician types a gas reading. If DNALab fails or returns `confidence = NONE`, inputs cannot be bounded precisely — see GASWIKI-10 for the limited-scope behaviour that follows.

**fuel_type** (proposed v2) CARRIED_AS **context only** — CONSUMED_BY **gaslab.dna_view.GasLabDnaView**
**altitude_band** (proposed v2) CARRIED_AS **context only** — CONSUMED_BY **gaslab.dna_view.GasLabDnaView**
**confidence** GATED_BY **CONCEPT_SCOPE_SHRINKAGE** (GASWIKI-10)

# 2. Combustion Foundations

> **Chunk summary.** Stoichiometry, lambda, the Brettschneider equation and its reliability/uncertainty model, the catalyst window, the two-truths frame, combustion-integrity metrics, RPM buckets, Euro-category threshold scaling, and the effect of E5/E10 + altitude on idle readings.
## 2.1 The ideal reaction {#CONCEPT_IDEAL_REACTION}
2 C₈H₁₈ + 25 O₂  →  16 CO₂ + 18 H₂O   (+ atmospheric N₂ carried through)
| **NOₓ** (thermal NO) | Combustion temperature exceeded ~2500 °F (~1370 °C), forcing N₂ + O₂ → NO |
## 2.2 Stoichiometry and lambda {#CONCEPT_LAMBDA}
Stoichiometric AFR for pump petrol ≈ **14.71 : 1** by mass. Lambda is a fuel-independent normalisation: `λ = AFR_actual / AFR_stoichiometric`.
- `λ = 1.000` → perfect chemical balance.
- `λ < 1.000` → rich (excess fuel); `λ > 1.000` → lean (excess air).
- `λ = 1.050` → 5 % lean (a 5 % air leak shifts a true 1.000 to 1.050).
GASLab uses λ as the universal mixture axis. AFR is reported for context (`AFR = λ × 14.71`) but never as the primary metric.
## 2.3 The Brettschneider lambda equation {#CONCEPT_BRETTSCHNEIDER}
[CO₂] + [CO]/2 + [O₂]
HC_FACTOR = 0.0025   (ppm HC → effective vol % in the carbon balance)
λ_5gas = λ₄ + (NOₓ_ppm / 1e6) × 0.5 / volumetric_sum_fraction
T-GASA-11 — `([CO₂] + [CO]/2 + [O₂] + (Hcv/4 · [CO₂]/([CO₂]+[CO])) · [CO₂]) / ([CO₂] + [CO] + [HC])` — is **not** a
definition: it has no `(1 + Hcv/4 …)` denominator normalisation and gives λ ≈ 1.45 for a stoichiometric sample
(F-C2-14). Adopting the full Brettschneider equation (with `Hcv` and the normalised denominator) would move every
verdict; it is a deferred design row (T-GASA-F14).

`Hcv` is the hydrogen-to-carbon ratio of the fuel (≈ 1.85 for pump petrol; 4 for methane); λ₄ does not use it. NOₓ contributes a small O₂-equivalence term (~0.05 % per 1 000 ppm NOₓ) supplied directly by the 5-gas analyser. Implementation note: `brettschneider.py` uses `hc_equiv = hc * 0.0025`, a standard and valid NDIR-scaling approach `[v2: q1]`.

- **λ is misfire-immune.** Raw fuel and raw air escaping a misfiring cylinder remain in chemical balance, so λ ≈ 1.000 even with HC spiking and CO₂ collapsing. Misfire detection therefore uses HC + CO₂ + NOₓ, not λ.
- **λ is air-leak sensitive.** A 5 % ambient dilution shifts a true 1.000 to 1.050. Air leaks MUST be ruled out before any "lean" verdict — the triangle gate (→ GATE_TRIANGLE) is the first defence.
## 2.4 Brettschneider reliability — λ is a property of the sample, not the engine {#CONCEPT_BRETTSCHNEIDER_RELIABILITY}

`[v2: q1, q2]` Brettschneider is mathematically robust but frequently misread as a direct measure of in-cylinder combustion "ground truth." It is an **exhaust-gas mass-balance equation**: given valid concentrations it yields a mathematically accurate λ *for that gas sample*. Whether that equals the engine's true stoichiometry depends entirely on **sample-stream integrity**. Garbage in, garbage out.

| **Misfire** (raised O₂ + HC) | Stable, near target | **High.** The equation accounts for unburned HC and excess O₂ and balances them back toward stoichiometry. λ stays ≈ 1.0 while raw HC spikes — read HC/O₂ separately, not λ, to see the misfire. λ only drifts if the ECU is actively trimming fuel off a wideband sensor. |

- **Instrument:** a well-calibrated 5-gas analyser holds λ to roughly **±0.05–0.10 absolute**; a drifted O₂ cell breaks the calculation. Headline equation accuracy is often quoted as **~±1 %** when inputs are clean.

- **Sample integrity (the ground-truth killer):** in a verified-sealed system Brettschneider is the gold standard. In a repair-bay with an unverified exhaust system, a leak can swing λ by **0.05–0.15 (5–15 % false-lean)**.

- **HC carbon-mass modelling:** the standard NDIR factor under-measures true carbon mass in gasoline exhaust by up to ~50 %, motivating the "Modified Brettschneider" (HC factor 12 instead of 6) for higher accuracy. GASLab's current scaling is documented and acceptable; the modified form is noted for future calibration only.

**Strategy rule:** treat λ as a measure of the *sample*. If λ ≈ 1.0 but HC is high → misfire. If λ shifts leaner at idle than at high idle → suspect a leak upstream of the probe. Never calibrate engine fuelling from tailpipe λ without first verifying ~0 % exhaust leakage. The leak-vs-sampling-error resolution lives at → TEST_PROBE_OCCLUSION and → CONCEPT_DIVERGENCE_MAGNITUDE (GASWIKI-04).
## 2.5 The catalyst window {#CONCEPT_CATALYST_WINDOW}
| Peak efficiency | 0.995 – 1.005 | All three TWC reactions > 99 % conversion |
| Light-off window | 0.98 – 1.02 | Cat reaches operating temperature and stays active |
| NOₓ breakthrough | λ > 1.03 | Rh sites saturated by O₂; reduction stops |
| CO / HC breakthrough | λ < 0.97 | Stored O₂ depleted; oxidation stops |

A working catalyst raises Combustion Efficiency from ~95 % engine-out to > 99 % tailpipe; the same scrubbing can also mask a feed-gas fault upstream of the cat (→ CONCEPT_HEALTHY_CAT_MASKING, GASWIKI-07 §7.8). Outside the light-off band the catalyst is, in effect, a hollow can. Catalyst diagnosis detail → CONCEPT_TWC and → TEST_DUAL_IDLE_CATALYST (GASWIKI-07).
## 2.6 The two simultaneous truths {#CONCEPT_TWO_TRUTHS}

Every gas diagnosis has two axes: **Balance** (λ axis — was the O₂-to-combustibles ratio correct?) and **Quality** (HC + CO₂ axis — did the molecules react?). A misfire is correct on balance (λ ≈ 1.0) but catastrophic on quality (HC spikes, CO₂ collapses). A vacuum leak is wrong on balance and may or may not affect quality. A one-axis verdict is half-blind. The fault atlas (GASWIKI-05/06A/06B) names which combination each `chemical_state` represents.
## 2.7 RPM measurement points {#CONCEPT_RPM_BUCKET}
| `STABILIZED_IDLE` | 650 – 900 | warm idle, closed-loop, 60 s settle |
| `REGULATORY_HIGH_IDLE` | 2200 – 2800 (commonly 2500) | SAE J1667 / BAR Two-Speed Idle |
| `STRESS_IDLE` | 3500 – 4500, VIN-dependent | clinical diagnostic point |

The bucket affects HC and NOₓ thresholds (turbulence improves the burn; cat heats up at higher RPM). Cold open-loop samples are **rejected** by the operating envelope — no cold-start enrichment fault class exists in v1/v2. The idle→2500 RPM transition is also the engine of the RPM-differential discriminators (oil-burn sub-modes, GDI carbon, timing) — see → TEST_RPM_SEPARATION_MATRIX (GASWIKI-08).
## 2.8 Euro-scaled thresholds {#CONCEPT_EURO_SCALING}

Numeric thresholds in the atlas are stated for a baseline Euro 4 vehicle with a working three-way cat. When DNA supplies `euro_emission_category` and per-vehicle CoC bounds, GASLab tightens or loosens:
| Euro | CO ceiling (idle, with cat) | HC ceiling (2500 RPM) | Source |
| EURO 1 | 4.5 % | — | type-approval limits |
| EURO 2 | 0.5 % | 1200 ppm | type-approval limits |
| EURO 3 | 0.3 % | 200 ppm | UK MOT |
| EURO 4 | 0.2 % | 200 ppm | UK MOT |
| EURO 5 | 0.2 % | 200 ppm | type-approval (2009–2010, upper edge of scope) |
When `confidence = HIGH` the per-vehicle CoC bounds override these defaults; see GASWIKI-10. (Euro 6/7 are out of the 1990–2010 scope and intentionally omitted.)
## 2.9 Fuel formulation and altitude {#CONCEPT_FUEL_ALTITUDE}
`[v2: q9]` Fuel blend and altitude shift idle readings enough to cause lean/rich misclassification if ignored.

- **Ethanol (E5/E10).** Blending ethanol consistently **lowers idle HC and CO** versus straight gasoline (oxygenated fuel burns cleaner). A car on E10 can read naturally lower HC/CO than the same car on pure petrol.
- **Effect on the triangle.** Lower HC/CO drag the dilution-screen sum and can nudge the Exhaust-Gas-Triangle sum (CO+CO₂+O₂) toward the lower edge — a near-14 % sample can tip into `INVALID`.

1. **Do NOT relax the triangle gate** (`SUM_VALID_MIN = 14.0`) for high-ethanol or high-altitude samples. It is a critical sample-integrity gate; re-validate with other data (e.g. OBD trims, probe-occlusion test) instead of widening it.

2. The `NORMAL_OPERATION` bounds *may* be widened slightly to absorb ethanol shifts, accepting some loss of sensitivity to subtle mixture faults — a deliberate, documented trade-off, not a gate change.
3. `fuel_type` and `altitude_band` are carried as **context only** (→ CONCEPT_GASLABDNAVIEW). They annotate the diagnosis; they do not move the validity boundary.
## 2.10 Combustion-integrity metrics {#CONCEPT_COMBUSTION_INTEGRITY}

`[v2.3: EP-GAS-03 / F-GAS-04, F-GAS-05]` The two-truths frame (→ CONCEPT_TWO_TRUTHS) needs one numeric handle for **Quality** and one explicit O₂-vs-CO discriminator for the rich/misfire split. Both are derived from the same five gases already in the sample; neither adds a new analyser channel or payload field.
healthy               >= ~0.95
combustion deficit     < ~0.95
Worked anchors from the warm-idle reference (GASWIKI-11 §11.2.1):
| Healthy idle | ≈ 14.7 % | ≈ 0.6 % | ≈ 0.96 | carbon mostly oxidised |
| Severe rich / incomplete burn | ≈ 10.0 % | ≈ 5.0 % | ≈ 0.67 | major combustion deficit |
**Oxygen usage** is the qualitative O₂-vs-CO discriminator behind the CO↔O₂ seesaw (→ RULE_SEESAW) and the HC/O₂/CO truth table (→ RULE_HC_O2_CO_TRUTH_TABLE):
high CO + O₂ ≈ 0       -> pure RICH over-fuelling
**CONCEPT_LAMBDA** EVALUATES_STATE_OF **fuel-air mixture** (λ = AFR_actual / AFR_stoichiometric, ≈ 14.71:1)
**CONCEPT_CATALYST_WINDOW** GATED_BY **λ 0.995–1.005** (peak efficiency), **λ 0.98–1.02** (light-off)
**CONCEPT_CATALYST_WINDOW** DESCRIBES **NOₓ breakthrough at λ > 1.03**, **CO/HC breakthrough at λ < 0.97**
**CONCEPT_RPM_BUCKET** GATED_BY **STABILIZED_IDLE** (650–900), **REGULATORY_HIGH_IDLE** (2200–2800), **STRESS_IDLE** (3500–4500)

# 3. The Five Gases
## 3.1 HC — Hydrocarbons (ppm) {#GAS_HC}

Unburned fuel. Rule of thumb: 1 % wasted fuel ≈ 200 ppm HC. Spikes when combustion is interrupted (misfire, lean misfire, leakage past valves/rings, EGR over-dilution) or when raw fuel is delivered without burning.
**Sensor:** NDIR tuned to the C–H absorption band ~3.4 µm. Heavy oil hydrocarbons read with reduced response — oil consumption can look smaller than it is.
| Tailpipe, working three-way cat | ≤ 35 ppm (≤ 50 ppm tolerable) |
| Tailpipe, no catalyst | ≤ 250 ppm |
| Pre-cat (engine-out), healthy engine | ≤ 100 ppm |

**Behaviour bands:** ≤ 50 ppm clean/active-cat; 50–250 ppm minor inefficiency or pre-cat normal; 250–800 ppm real combustion problem; 800–2000 ppm severe misfire / oil burning / cat failure; > 2000 ppm almost always mechanical or hard ignition fault.
## 3.2 CO — Carbon monoxide (vol %) {#GAS_CO}
Partial-oxidation product. CO exists only if combustion happened but ran out of oxygen. **One-way rich indicator:** CO ≈ 0 does not prove lean, but CO > ~1.5 % effectively guarantees rich.
**Sensor:** NDIR ~4.7 µm with chemical filters to suppress H₂ interference. Electrochemical CO cells over-read on H₂ from rich combustion; NDIR is mandatory for diagnostic-grade work.
| Tailpipe, working cat | 0.1 – 0.45 % |
| Tailpipe, cat not lighting off | 0.5 – 0.9 % |
| Pre-cat | up to 1.5 % can be normal |
**Behaviour bands:** ≤ 0.5 % stoich/clean-up; 0.5–1.5 % mild rich or normal pre-cat; 1.5–3 % clear rich; > 3 % very rich (expect concurrent HC rise).
**Post-cat rule.** With a working cat at idle, CO < 0.3 %. Closed-loop control reported yet tailpipe CO > 0.8 % ⇒ catalyst failing or poisoned.
## 3.3 CO₂ — Carbon dioxide (vol %) {#GAS_CO2}
End product of *complete* combustion — the "north star" of efficiency. Anything that disturbs combustion drops CO₂ below its ~15.5 % ceiling. CO₂ forms a bell curve against λ, peaking at λ ≈ 1.000.
**Sensor:** NDIR ~4.3 µm. Highly stable, primary efficiency reference.
| Working cat | 14.5 – 16.0 % |
| Cat not lighting off | 13.5 – 14.5 % |
| Without catalyst | ≥ 13 % |
| Mild combustion deficit | 11 – 13 % |
| Severe combustion failure | < 11 % |

CO₂ typically rises 1–2 % from idle to 2500 RPM as turbulence improves the burn — a CO₂ that *falls* with revs is a red flag. If CO₂ < 13 % the reasoning must explain *why* — CO₂ collapse never happens on its own.
## 3.4 O₂ — Oxygen (vol %) {#GAS_O2}
Free oxygen remaining after combustion. Ambient air is 20.9 %; a healthy idle tailpipe is ≤ 1.5 % (≤ 0.35 % post-cat). O₂ climbs sharply once λ > 1.
| Working cat, stoich | ≤ 0.35 % |
| Working cat, edge of light-off | 0.3 – 0.7 % |
| No catalyst | 0.5 – 1.5 % |

**Behaviour bands:** < 0.5 % rich or perfect stoich; 0.5–1.5 % typical pre-cat or mild lean; 1.5–4 % clearly lean or misfire; > 4 % severe lean, big misfire, or air leak; ≈ 20.9 % with HC=0, CO=0, CO₂≈0.04 % ⇒ no combustion (cranking / probe out).
ΔO₂ per misfiring cylinder ≈ 21 % / cylinder_count
One dead cylinder on a 4-cyl ≈ 5.25 % O₂ rise; 6-cyl ≈ 3.5 %; 8-cyl ≈ 2.6 %. `cylinder_count` comes from `GasLabDnaView`.
## 3.5 NOₓ — Oxides of nitrogen (ppm) {#GAS_NOX}

Thermal NO formation requires peak temperatures > ~2500 °F (~1370 °C). At idle without load, NOₓ ≈ 0. Peaks **under load** near stoichiometric; suppressed by rich mixtures (cooling) and EGR (inert dilution).
| Idle, warm, healthy | < 100 ppm |
| Idle, elevated | 100 – 500 ppm |
| High-idle (2500 RPM), healthy | 100 – 1000 ppm |
| Under load, healthy | 500 – 1500 ppm |
| Under load, EGR / cooling / timing fault | > 1500 ppm |
## 3.6 The 5-gas cheat sheet {#CONCEPT_5GAS_CHEATSHEET}
| Hydrocarbons | HC | 0 – 35 ppm | Moderate | Low | Very high (> 1000 ppm) |
| Carbon monoxide | CO | 0.1 – 0.45 % | High (> 1.0 %) | Very low (< 0.1 %) | Low – moderate |
| Carbon dioxide | CO₂ | 14.5 – 16.0 % | Low (< 12 %) | Low (< 12 %) | Very low (< 10 %) |
| Nitric oxide | NOₓ | < 100 ppm | Very low | Very high | Low |
## 3.7 Sensor cross-sensitivity reference {#CONCEPT_CROSS_SENSITIVITY}
| CO | H₂ | 100 ppm | < 50 % | False high |
| CO | H₂S | 5 ppm | < 0.1 % | Minimal (filtered) |
| NO₂ | H₂S | 5 ppm | < −80 % | False low (negative) |
| NO | H₂S | 5 ppm | < 20 % | False high |
| NO | NO₂ | 5 ppm | < 7 % | False high |

# 4. Inter-Gas Grammar & Validity Gates

> **Chunk summary.** Chemistry-level validity gates first, then the reasoning rules and named overrides. Two v2 additions: how to tell a real pre-cat air leak from a sampling-apparatus leak, and how far tailpipe chemistry diverges from ECU perception per fault.
### 4.1 The Exhaust Gas Triangle (Rule of 16 / Rule of 15) {#GATE_TRIANGLE}
In a clean petrol burn the sum `[CO] + [CO₂] + [O₂] ≈ 14 – 16 %` is **invariant** regardless of mixture — the reaction shuffles oxygen between CO and CO₂; the total stays the same.
| 14.0 – 16.0 | `VALID` | proceed |
| 16.0 – 18.0 | `EXTERNAL_O2_SUSPECT` | warn + run; downstream rules still evaluate |
| < 14.0 | `INVALID` | halt — `chemical_state = SAMPLE_INVALID` |
| > 18.0 | `INVALID` | halt — likely ambient-air probe / sensor fault |

This is the **only** gate that can halt evaluation outright. The sum drifts outside [14,16] only via (a) ambient-air dilution (sum rises past 16) or (b) probe-insertion failure (sum collapses or spikes to ambient). **Do not relax `SUM_VALID_MIN = 14.0`** for ethanol blends or altitude (→ CONCEPT_FUEL_ALTITUDE) — re-validate with other data instead.
### 4.2 The dilution screen {#GATE_DILUTION}
Rapid sanity check: `[CO] + [CO₂] > 6 %`. An undiluted sample always satisfies it; ≤ 6 % indicates heavy dilution.
### 4.3 The cranking / ambient-air shape {#GATE_CRANKING_SHAPE}

HC ≈ 0, CO ≈ 0, CO₂ ≈ 0.04 %, O₂ ≈ 20.9 % gives a triangle sum ≈ 20.94 %. At a running-engine bucket the triangle rejects it as `INVALID` (the envelope requires a warm running engine). At the `CRANKING` bucket (a `will_not_start` session) the triangle and dilution gates do not run: no combustion is the finding, not a probe fault (→ RULE_CRANKING).
### 4.4 Pre-cat air leak vs sample-handling error {#CONCEPT_LEAK_VS_SAMPLING}

`[v2: q3]` The signature **low CO + elevated O₂ + low HC** is classic *dilution* — and a physical exhaust leak (cracked manifold, failed flex pipe) is **chemically identical** to a sampling-apparatus leak (loose probe, leaking hose). Both inject ~20.9 % O₂ atmospheric air.

**Key limitation:** while the triangle sum is still inside 14–18 %, the analyser **cannot** distinguish the two from gas data alone. The gate confirms the gas is "exhaust-like"; it cannot confirm the exhaust solely represents the engine's output. Resolution needs a **second source of truth** — OBD fuel trims — plus a mechanical check:
| STFT (OBD) | Positive — ECU adding fuel | Normal (≈ 0 % / oscillating) |

**Protocol.** (1) High analyser O₂ → read STFT. Positive STFT ⇒ engine truly lean / leak is **physical**. STFT ≈ 0 with high analyser O₂ ⇒ leak is in the **sampling apparatus**. (2) Confirm with the **probe-occlusion test** (→ TEST_PROBE_OCCLUSION, GASWIKI-08): block the probe tip; the pump should stall and O₂ should drop to near 0. If it doesn't, the sampling system leaks. The escalation that follows a triangle breach lives at → FAULT_EXHAUST_AIR_LEAK (GASWIKI-05).
### 4.5 The CO ↔ O₂ seesaw {#RULE_SEESAW}
- CO up, O₂ down → rich; CO down (≈ 0), O₂ up → lean.

- **CO up AND O₂ up together → COLLISION** — physically impossible in a single balanced event. Two explanations: rich-side fuel dump with partial misfire, or downstream air ingress. Disambiguated by the triangle (→ GATE_TRIANGLE): sum ≈ 15 ⇒ rich misfire; sum > 16 ⇒ ingress.
The quantified form of this discriminator lives at → CONCEPT_COMBUSTION_INTEGRITY (GASWIKI-02 §2.10); keep the formula there so this section remains the rule grammar.
### 4.6 The HC + O₂ + CO truth table {#RULE_HC_O2_CO_TRUTH_TABLE}
The O₂-vs-CO reasoning behind the misfire/rich split is summarised at → CONCEPT_COMBUSTION_INTEGRITY (GASWIKI-02 §2.10), without adding a separate numeric ratio threshold.
### 4.7 The HC ↔ NOₓ anti-correlation near stoichiometry {#RULE_HC_NOX_ANTICORR}
### 4.8 The masking rule (named override) {#RULE_MASKING}
HC > 1000 ppm  AND  O₂ > 3.0 %  AND  NOₓ < 50 ppm
No combustion → no heat → no NOₓ despite the air looking lean. **Priority 85** (above all lean/rich rules at 80).
### 4.9 The collision rule (named override) {#RULE_COLLISION}
CO > tier_max  AND  O₂ > 2.0 %
AND triangle 14 – 16 %  ⇒  RICH_MISFIRE
AND triangle > 16 %     ⇒  EXHAUST_AIR_LEAK (downstream ingress on rich)
**Priority 80.**
### 4.10 The cam-timing rule (named override) {#RULE_WVT}

`[v2.1: q7]` Retargeted from the retired single `WRONG_VALVE_TIMING` to the three system-specific cam-timing states (→ FAULT_CAM_TIMING_RETARDED_MAF, → FAULT_CAM_TIMING_ADVANCED, → FAULT_CAM_TIMING_RETARDED_MAP, GASWIKI-06B). Pure rich and pure lean cannot explain HC + CO + O₂ all elevated — mechanical, not fuel-mixture.
# Lean / mixed branch — Priority 82 (above collision, below masking)
HC > 1000 ppm  AND  CO present  AND  O₂ > 2.0 %
→ O₂ 2.0–4.5 %, λ 1.08–1.18, signature PERSISTS at 2500 RPM   ⇒ CAM_TIMING_RETARDED_MAF
→ O₂ 1.2–2.5 %, λ 1.03–1.08, NOₓ RISES at 2500 RPM            ⇒ CAM_TIMING_ADVANCED
# Rich branch (Speed-Density over-fuelling) — Priority 40 fallback
AND signature PARTIALLY normalises toward 2500 RPM            ⇒ CAM_TIMING_RETARDED_MAP
(disambiguated from RICH_MIXTURE by the RPM-normalisation tell + OBD trims −27…−45 %)

> Ontology / code note: the ontology (`gas_lab_ontology.yaml` WVT rule) and `resolution.py` currently emit the single `WRONG_VALVE_TIMING` on `HC > 1000` and `O₂ > 5.0%`. Re-binding this rule to the three `CAM_TIMING_*` states (and the rich-branch RPM-normalisation discriminator) is part of the coordinated cross-lab change in → GAS_VOCABULARY §21; superseding the older T-DOC-13 row 18 note.
### 4.11 The λ-mismatch (truth-vs-perception) rule {#RULE_LAMBDA_MISMATCH}
| ≤ 0.05 | Sensors agree — proceed |
| 0.05 – 0.08 | Borderline — investigate fuel trims and exhaust leak first |
| > 0.08 | Mismatch — raise the truth-vs-perception override |

Most likely candidates: upstream O₂ sensor skewed, exhaust leak upstream of the sensor, ECU calibration drift. This surfaces as `O2_SENSOR_BIASED_LOW` / `_HIGH` in the atlas (→ FAULT_O2_SENSOR_BIASED_LOW, GASWIKI-05).
### 4.12 ECU-vs-tailpipe divergence magnitudes {#CONCEPT_DIVERGENCE_MAGNITUDE}

`[v2: q6]` The λ-mismatch detector needs to know how *much* divergence each fault produces — if divergence is usually small the detector has little to work with. Empirically (1990–2010 petrol) divergence is common and frequently large, because the onboard O₂/AFR sensor measures only oxygen and is biased by physical/chemical degradation, whereas Brettschneider balances all five gases.

| **Ignition misfire** | up to **Δλ ≈ 0.24** | O₂ spike (~4 % pre-cat, 6-cyl single miss) reads "false lean"; early-era ECUs chase it, adding up to 30–77 % fuel. Tailpipe truth: actual λ ≈ 0.76–0.85 (rich). |
| **O₂-sensor poisoning / signal bias** | **Δλ ≈ 0.15 – 0.23** | Silicone/silicate/oil contamination skews sensor voltage low (lean); ECU enriches. Tailpipe truth: λ ≈ 0.77–0.85, CO often 5–8 %. |
| **Upstream exhaust air leak** | **Δλ ≈ 0.05 – 0.10** | Tramp O₂ drives sensor lean; ECU enriches ~5 % to re-centre → actual λ ≈ 0.950 against a reported 1.000. |

| **Wideband calibration-resistor damage** (late-2000s LSU 4.2/4.9) | **Δλ ≈ 0.12 – 0.18** | Corroded pins / damaged trim resistor break the current-to-λ curve; probe may report 1.30 while actual is 1.10, or 0.82 while actual is 0.95 — erratic over-correction. |

**Reading:** a measured Δλ between chemistry and ECU is not noise — it sizes the fault. Δλ ≈ 0.05–0.10 with normal-looking gases points to a leak; Δλ > 0.15 with high CO points to sensor bias or chased misfire. Cross-check against the gas vector before naming the bias direction.
### 4.13 Cross-channel sanity rails {#RULE_SANITY_RAILS}
- HC/CO/CO₂/O₂ must be physically consistent: triangle sum 14–16 % at idle. Outside that ⇒ sensor problem, air leak, or analyser drift.
- λ from analyser within ±0.08 of ECU's λ is normal; wider raises perception-contradiction (→ RULE_LAMBDA_MISMATCH).
- Idle NOₓ > ~1000 ppm is suspicious — confirm load, EGR, cooling.
- Trims (STFT/LTFT) outside ±25 % at idle indicate a real large mixture issue or sensor rail-out — OBDLab's job, surfaced to COMLab.
### 4.14 The cranking-shape rule {#RULE_CRANKING}
At the `CRANKING` bucket only (GAS_VOCABULARY §7), GASLab skips §4.1 and §4.2 and classifies the sample in this order:
| CO₂ ≥ 8.0 | `SAMPLE_INVALID` (running-engine combustion contradicts the no-start) | `INVALID` |
| CO ≥ 1.5 (GAS_VOCABULARY §10.2 `clear_rich.min`) | `RICH_MISFIRE` (fuel arrives, does not burn: flooded) | `VALID` |
| CO₂ < 5.0 (GAS_VOCABULARY §10.3 `total_quench.max`) | `LEAN_MISFIRE` (no fuel, or too little fuel, burns) | `VALID` |
| otherwise (5.0 ≤ CO₂ < 8.0) | `INCOMPLETE_COMBUSTION` (some combustion, the engine does not run) | `VALID` |
COMLab's `non_starter` rules NS-001..NS-003 gate on these three states. The four running-engine buckets keep §4.1 and §4.2 unchanged.

# 5. Fault Signature Atlas — Part A

> **Chunk summary.** Sixteen `chemical_state` entities. Each is a typed record (gas vector + DNA gate + match class + discriminator + cross-refs). Numeric thresholds are normative; directional patterns are the lookup key. `match_class` feeds the confidence ceiling (→ CONCEPT_CONFIDENCE_CEILING, GASWIKI-10).
- **gas_vector:** HC normal–moderate | CO **> 1.5 %** | CO₂ < 13 % | O₂ **< 0.5 %** | NOₓ very low | λ **< 0.95**
- **gas_vector:** HC low (< 300 ppm) | CO **< 0.1 %** | CO₂ < 13 % | O₂ **> 2.5 %** | NOₓ very high under load | λ **> 1.05**
- **gas_vector:** HC **> 1000 ppm** | CO normal–low | CO₂ **< 10 %** | O₂ **> 3.0 %** | NOₓ **< 50 ppm** | λ ≥ 1.0 (false-lean)

- **discriminator:** masking rule fires. `inferred_misfiring_cylinder_count ≈ round(O₂ / (21 / cylinder_count))`. Note `[v2: q6]`: ECU may chase the O₂ spike with up to 30–77 % added fuel — chemistry λ stays misfire-immune while perception swings; expect a large Δλ (→ CONCEPT_DIVERGENCE_MAGNITUDE).
- **gas_vector:** HC 200–600 ppm | CO **< 0.2 %** | CO₂ < 12 % | O₂ **> 4 %** | NOₓ variable | λ **> 1.15**
- **discriminator:** if NOₓ also high (> 500 ppm) suspect EGR failure or oil burning (chamber hot enough to make NOₓ despite lean).
- **gas_vector:** HC high | CO **> 1.0 %** | CO₂ low | O₂ **> 2.0 %** | NOₓ low | λ < 1.0
- **discriminator:** collision pattern (CO and O₂ both high). Triangle disambiguates: sum > 16 % ⇒ ingress (→ FAULT_EXHAUST_AIR_LEAK); sum ≈ 15.5 % ⇒ rich misfire.
- **gas_vector:** HC normal | CO normal | CO₂ low | O₂ **> 2 %** | NOₓ low | λ falsely **> 1.05**

- **discriminator:** triangle sum < 14 % or > 16 % is the smoking gun. λ reads lean because Brettschneider sees ambient O₂ dilution; HC/CO unaffected (leak is downstream of combustion). **v2:** a physical leak and a sampling-apparatus leak look identical here — resolve via OBD STFT + probe occlusion (→ CONCEPT_LEAK_VS_SAMPLING, → TEST_PROBE_OCCLUSION).
- **gas_vector:** HC normal | CO normal | CO₂ normal–high | O₂ normal | NOₓ **> 1000 ppm** under load | λ ≈ 1.0
- **gas_vector:** HC > 200 ppm | CO > 1.0 % | CO₂ < 12 % | O₂ variable | NOₓ > 500 ppm | λ variable

- **discriminator:** triangle sum outside [14, 18]. Probe not seated, exhaust leak, analyser drift, water condensation, or ambient air. The only value where `sample_validity = INVALID`. Refuse to diagnose; instruct re-prime.
- **gas_vector (idle):** HC slight increase (120–250 ppm) | CO slight (0.10–0.30 %) | CO₂ 11.5–13 % | O₂ 0.8–1.5 % | NOₓ 20–60 | λ 1.01–1.04
- **gas_vector (2500 RPM):** NOₓ **very high (> 1200 ppm)**, others near normal | λ ≈ 1.0–1.06

- **discriminator** `[v2: q7]`: the signature is **RPM-dependent** — at idle thermal energy is low so NOₓ barely moves; at 2500 RPM under load peak temps exceed ~2500 °F and NOₓ spikes hard while the closed loop holds λ ≈ 1.0 with normal MAP. Distinct from → FAULT_HIGH_COMBUSTION_TEMP by the clean idle and the NOₓ-only high-idle spike. Pinging often audible. Carbon deposits / head machining raise effective compression and mimic this. Distinct from the *cam*-timing family (→ FAULT_CAM_TIMING_ADVANCED, → FAULT_CAM_TIMING_RETARDED_MAP, → FAULT_CAM_TIMING_RETARDED_MAF, GASWIKI-06B), which show rough idle and a λ offset *at idle* rather than a clean idle with a NOₓ-only high-idle spike.
- **gas_vector (2500 RPM):** HC 250–600 ppm | CO₂ 9–11.5 % | NOₓ near zero | λ 1.04–1.12

- **discriminator** `[v2: q7]`: late combustion continues into the exhaust stroke — peak temp and NOₓ collapse, EGT rises, cat/pipe run hot. The excess unreacted O₂ shifts the **calculated** λ artificially lean even though delivered AFR is stoichiometric (a chemistry-reads-lean / engine-is-fine case). HC stays high across both speeds; NOₓ stays near zero at both. Check base timing, cam timing, CKP sensor. This is the *ignition*-retard signature; a mechanically retarded *cam* routes instead to → FAULT_CAM_TIMING_RETARDED_MAP (rich) or → FAULT_CAM_TIMING_RETARDED_MAF (lean) per the load-calc system (GASWIKI-06B).
### FAULT_O2_SENSOR_BIASED_LOW — sensor under-reads O₂, ECU enriches {#FAULT_O2_SENSOR_BIASED_LOW}
- **chemical_state:** `O2_SENSOR_BIASED_LOW` · **dna_gate:** none · **match_class:** SPECIFIC (DEFINITIVE when → RULE_LAMBDA_MISMATCH fires)
- **gas_vector:** HC slight increase | CO **moderate–high increase** | CO₂ slight decrease | O₂ **low** | NOₓ slight decrease | λ(chem) **< 1.0 (rich)**

- **discriminator:** sensor signals less O₂ than present; ECU enriches. Chemistry λ rich while ECU perceives lean — truth-vs-perception mismatch, positive fuel trims on scan tool. `[v2: q6]` expect Δλ ≈ 0.15–0.23 with CO frequently 5–8 %. Causes: contamination, ageing, heater-circuit failure.

- **silicone-poisoning sub-case** `[v2.2: casesextra]`: Si from RTV sealant / silicone sprays / silicate coolant glazes the zirconia element and **locks the sensor at ~0.10–0.15 V (stuck lean, switch-rate < 4 / 10 s)** — distinct from a *lazy* sensor, which still switches. The ECU pegs trims (STFT/LTFT **> +15 %**), driving the engine severely rich (**λ(chem) ≈ 0.86, CO 4–5 %, HC ~400 ppm**) while it sets a **lean DTC (P0171)** — a **negative δλ** (gas richer than OBD, e.g. λ_gas 0.86 vs λ_OBD 1.07). The same agent then migrates to the cat → see → CONCEPT_CATALYST_POISONING_AGENTS (GASWIKI-07, Si row). Inspect the sensor tip for white/grey glassy deposit; the catalyst may already be thermally damaged. Source: `casesextra` Case 8.
### FAULT_O2_SENSOR_BIASED_HIGH — sensor over-reads O₂, ECU leans out {#FAULT_O2_SENSOR_BIASED_HIGH}
- **chemical_state:** `O2_SENSOR_BIASED_HIGH` · **dna_gate:** none · **match_class:** SPECIFIC (DEFINITIVE when → RULE_LAMBDA_MISMATCH fires)
- **gas_vector:** HC slight increase | CO **low** | CO₂ slight decrease | O₂ slight increase | NOₓ slight increase | λ(chem) **> 1.0 (lean)**

- **discriminator:** opposite of biased-low. Chemistry λ lean while ECU perceives rich — negative fuel trims. Wiring ground offset can also shift sensor voltage high. Late-era wideband calibration-resistor damage can produce erratic large Δλ (0.12–0.18) `[v2: q6]`.
- **gas_vector:** HC slight–moderate increase (150–300 ppm) | CO slight increase | CO₂ slight decrease (11–13 %) | O₂ **slight increase (1–2 %)** | NOₓ no change/slight decrease | λ ≈ 1.0–1.03

- **discriminator:** worn rings/valve seals reduce compression and efficiency across all cylinders. **No RPM cleanup** (rules out valve seals) and **no high-idle spike** (rules out isolated piston-ring blow-by) — flat, lazy, inefficient at both speeds. Distinguish from oil burning by absence of λ mismatch / cat poisoning; from misfire by absence of a large O₂ spike. Routing detail → FAULT_POA_SIGNATURE discriminator (GASWIKI-06A).

# 6A. Fault Atlas — Oil Burning & Mechanical Wear

> **Chunk summary.** The mechanical-wear and oil-ingestion entities, plus the single RPM-differential discriminator that resolves the `POA_SIGNATURE` catch-all to a specific leaf. v2 maps five field-documented oil-burn cases onto existing enum values and records candidate new values in → CONCEPT_PROPOSED_ENUM_ADDITIONS (GASWIKI-11).
- **gas_vector:** HC no change/slight decrease | CO **slight decrease** | CO₂ slight decrease | O₂ no change/slight decrease | NOₓ no change/slight decrease | λ ≈ 1.0
- **gas_vector:** HC **> 100 ppm at idle** | CO low–moderate | CO₂ low–moderate | O₂ **high** | NOₓ variable | λ **> 1.0 at idle → ≈ 1.0 at 2500 RPM**

- **discriminator:** no port-wash on GDI → carbon builds on valve backs; localised lean pockets create a lean-misfire look at idle that **clears substantially at 2500 RPM** as air velocity overcomes the restriction. True lean/vacuum-leak faults do not normalise the same way (→ TEST_RPM_SEPARATION_MATRIX). In-scope for 2000–2010 GDI vehicles only.
- **gas_vector:** HC high | CO **> 3.0 %** | CO₂ low | O₂ **very low** | NOₓ very low | λ **< 0.85**

- **discriminator:** ruptured FPR diaphragm lets raw liquid fuel into the manifold via the vacuum hose, bypassing injectors. **OBD differentiator:** STFT ≤ −20 %, LTFT ≤ −23 %, pegged at the floor with the rich condition still present (a stuck-open injector pushes trims negative too, but ECU correction partially reduces the rich reading; FPR's trims sit at the floor with zero effect). **Confirm:** disconnect the FPR vacuum hose engine-running — raw fuel/vapour present is conclusive.
- **gas_vector:** HC high | CO **> 3.0 %** | CO₂ low | O₂ **very low** | NOₓ very low | λ **< 0.85** (tailpipe identical to FPR rupture)

- **discriminator:** failed HPFP shaft seal admits high-pressure fuel into the oil sump; petrol-contaminated oil is drawn through PCV as unmetered vapour. Differentiator is **crankcase evidence**: dipstick fuel smell / level above max; abnormal positive crankcase-pressure deviation; fuel vapour/droplets at the PCV supply hose. **Severity:** stop-drive — fuel-diluted oil loses viscosity fast. In-scope for 2000–2010 GDI vehicles only.
### FAULT_WORN_VALVE_SEALS — idle-vacuum oil ingestion, clears at 2500 RPM {#FAULT_WORN_VALVE_SEALS}

- **physics:** high idle vacuum draws oil down the valve guides onto the intake-valve backs → elevated HC and a rich offset at idle (heavy oil acts as extra fuel). At 2500 RPM vacuum collapses, the oil siphon stops, residual oil burns off, cat heats → **rapid cleanup**. `[v2: q4]` the rich-offset-at-idle refinement (CO ~0.95 %, λ ~0.96) supersedes the v1 "trims stable, HC 75–250" range, which described a milder presentation; both are the same fault at different severities.
| Idle | 100–150 ppm | near normal | normal (~14 %) | < 0.5 % | low | ~ 1.0 | ~ 0 % |

- **physics:** under load, peak cylinder pressure forces combustion gas and vaporised oil past worn rings into the crankcase; PCV draws the oil-and-fuel vapour into the intake as unmetered fuel — genuine rich at the tailpipe, with the heavy oil thermally cracking and consuming chamber O₂. Negative trims at load + persistent rich distinguish this from simple over-fuelling. **Worsens with RPM** (opposite of valve seals). `[v2: q4]`
| Worn valve seals | High HC at idle that cleans up when revved; possible λ mismatch; P0420 |
| Severe oil burning | HC > 500 ppm persists across RPM, λ mismatch + P0420 |
| Catastrophic | HC > 2000 ppm, continuous λ mismatch, dead cat |
#### New oil-burn sub-modes (v2, mapped to existing enum) {#CONCEPT_OILBURN_SUBMODES}

`[v2: q4]` Five field-documented oil-ingestion modes. Per the v2 enum decision they are **mapped onto existing values now** (no contract break) and recorded as candidate new values in → CONCEPT_PROPOSED_ENUM_ADDITIONS (GASWIKI-11).
| Field case | Idle signature | 2500 RPM signature | Maps to (v2 emit) | Proposed v2.x value |
| Worn piston rings | HC 120, CO 0.15, λ 1.00 | HC 380, CO 0.85, λ 0.985 (worsens) | `WORN_PISTON_RINGS` | — (exists) |
| Degraded valve-stem seals | HC 450, CO 0.95, λ 0.96 | HC 65, λ 1.00 (cleans up) | `WORN_VALVE_SEALS` | — (exists) |
| Stuck-open PCV valve | HC 610, CO 1.90, λ 0.925 (heavy rich) | HC 170, CO 0.45, λ 0.988 | `POA_SIGNATURE` (clogged-PCV sub-mode) | `PCV_STUCK_OPEN` |

| Head-gasket oil-to-cylinder breach | HC 340, CO 0.65, O₂ 2.6, NOₓ 18, λ 1.085 (false lean) | HC 440, O₂ 2.1, NOₓ 38, λ 1.055 | `COOLANT_LEAK_INTERNAL` (oil+coolant breach, → GASWIKI-06B) | `HEAD_GASKET_OIL_BREACH` |
| Worn turbo turbine seals | HC 720, CO 0.07, λ 1.000 (stoich) | HC 130, λ 1.002 | `POA_SIGNATURE` (turbo-seal sub-mode); gate on `induction_type` forced | `TURBO_SEAL_OIL_LEAK` |

**Disambiguating logic** `[v2: q4]`: *high tailpipe HC with perfect stoichiometric λ and near-zero CO* ⇒ oil cracking **outside** the cylinder (turbo turbine seal) — combustion is intact, so it cannot be a mixture or misfire fault. *Heavy rich at closed-throttle idle that clears as manifold vacuum falls* ⇒ stuck-open PCV drawing crankcase oil aerosol. *False-lean O₂ with suppressed NOₓ and white steam* ⇒ coolant/oil head-gasket breach (route to `COOLANT_LEAK_INTERNAL`). Always **inspect/replace the PCV valve before authorising ring or short-block work** — a stuck-open PCV replicates severe ring-failure emissions at idle.
#### 6A.1 RPM-differential discriminator — resolving POA_SIGNATURE to a leaf {#CONCEPT_RPM_DIFFERENTIAL_DISCRIMINATOR}

`POA_SIGNATURE` is the catch-all an oil-burning sample lands on first. To emit the *specific* wear fault, compare the idle reading against the 2500 RPM reading and match the **HC change direction** plus load-state CO and fuel-trim columns. This is the single discriminator the atlas uses to route a catch-all oil hit to a leaf. **All thresholds are inherited from the cited sources — this table introduces no new numbers, only consolidates them for routing.**
| Route to | HC @ idle | HC @ 2500 | HC Δ | CO @ 2500 | Trims @ 2500 | λ | Source |
| `WORN_VALVE_SEALS` | 300–500 (rich offset) | ≤ 35 | **↓ sharply** | low | ± 8 % | 0.96→1.0 | FAULT_WORN_VALVE_SEALS |
| `WORN_PISTON_RINGS` | 100–150 | > 300 | **↑ stays elevated** | > 0.5 % | ≤ −12 % | →< 0.99 | FAULT_WORN_PISTON_RINGS |
| `WORN_ENGINE` | 150–300 | ~ unchanged | **flat** (no cleanup) | slight increase | ~ 0 % | 1.0–1.03 | FAULT_WORN_ENGINE |
| `POA_SIGNATURE` (turbo-seal) | > 500, CO ≈ 0 | drops | **↓** but λ stays 1.0 | ≈ 0 | ~ 0 % | **1.0 (stoich)** | turbo sub-mode above |
| `POA_SIGNATURE` (severe/catastrophic) | > 500 | > 500 (persists) | **flat, high** | variable | variable | λ mismatch | FAULT_POA_SIGNATURE |
| `COOLANT_LEAK_INTERNAL` | HC 200–400, O₂ > 2, NOₓ < 30 | persists, NOₓ stays < 30 | **flat** | elevated | — | false lean | GASWIKI-06B |

**Routing precedence:** sharp HC drop at 2500 ⇒ `WORN_VALVE_SEALS`; HC rising/elevated with negative trims and CO > 0.5 % under load ⇒ `WORN_PISTON_RINGS`; moderate HC that neither cleans up nor spikes, only generalised drift, no λ mismatch ⇒ `WORN_ENGINE`; extreme HC with stoich λ and ~0 CO ⇒ turbo-seal `POA_SIGNATURE`; HC > 500 persisting both states with λ mismatch ⇒ leave on `POA_SIGNATURE`; false-lean O₂ + suppressed NOₓ ⇒ `COOLANT_LEAK_INTERNAL`. The CO-@-idle and `RICH_MISFIRE` collision cases are disambiguated upstream (→ FAULT_RICH_MISFIRE, → RULE_COLLISION) before this discriminator runs.

> Fuel trim is a perception/DNA-context signal, **not** a 5-gas channel (vocabulary home: `GAS_VOCABULARY §10.8`). The HC change-direction and CO-@-2500 columns are the gas-visible primary discriminators; the trim column corroborates only when DNA context supplies it.

# 6B. Fault Atlas — Valvetrain, EGR, EVAP & Combustion-Quality

> **Chunk summary.** The remaining valvetrain / EGR / combustion-quality entities plus the consolidated 34-value lookup. v2 refinements: the cam-timing split into three system-specific states `[v2.1: q7]` (retired `WRONG_VALVE_TIMING`) and the head-gasket oil-to-cylinder breach sub-mode of coolant leak (q4).

> **v2.1 cam-timing taxonomy** `[v2.1: q7]` — the single `WRONG_VALVE_TIMING` value is retired and split into three system-specific states sourced from the q1&7 timings dossier. A physically retarded cam lowers pumping efficiency and raises MAP (low vacuum); the *emissions* fingerprint then depends on the load-calc system (Speed-Density inverts rich vs MAF lean), while an advanced cam presents the same mild-lean internal-EGR pattern on both systems. **Consumer for all three:** COMLab `chemical_state` routing / fault-atlas (this chunk). Tailpipe gas cannot prove cam *phase* on its own (that needs CKP/CMP correlation, OBDLab/DTCLab) → `match_class` SPECIFIC, not DEFINITIVE.

- **discriminator:** retarded cam → low vacuum / high MAP; a Speed-Density ECU reads the high MAP as load and over-fuels → pure-rich tailpipe. Overlaps → FAULT_RICH_MIXTURE chemically; the tell is **partial normalisation toward 2500 RPM** as vacuum recovers (λ 0.85–0.95, CO falls) whereas a sensor/fuelling rich-bias stays flat. OBD corroboration: total fuel trim −27 % to −45 % at idle, correcting to −18 % to −27 % at stress idle (OBDLab/DTCLab). DTC context P0016–P0019 is DTCLab territory.

- **discriminator:** reversion + late exhaust events leave unburned O₂; a MAF ECU reads lean → positive trims (+22 % to +42 %). **Separation from a vacuum leak:** a vacuum leak's lean / positive trims **normalise** at 2500 RPM (metered air dominates); this cam fault **persists or worsens** across the whole RPM band because the mechanical phasing error persists (→ TEST_RPM_SEPARATION_MATRIX).

- **discriminator:** advancing the cam opens/closes valves early and widens overlap → internal-EGR dilution → rough idle, HC up, mild CO. **No Speed-Density-vs-MAF inversion** (both systems present the same mild-lean idle). At 2500 RPM dynamic scavenging stabilises combustion (HC/CO fall) while NOₓ **rises** with peak pressure/temperature. Separation from → FAULT_TIMING_OVER_ADVANCED (ignition): advanced *cam* shows rough-idle HC + mild-lean λ at idle, not the clean idle / NOₓ-only high-idle spike of ignition over-advance.
- **gas_vector:** HC normal | CO normal | CO₂ normal | O₂ normal | NOₓ **> 1000 ppm under load**

- **dual-idle NOₓ-escalation signature** `[v2.2: casesextra]`: with zero recirculation, peak combustion temperature climbs hard with RPM. NOₓ steps from **~1200 ppm at idle to > 2500–3000 ppm at 2500 RPM (Δ > 1500 ppm is decisive)** while **HC and CO stay pristine throughout** (combustion is complete; there is simply no thermal suppression). DTC context P0401. **Polarity caution** `[v2.2: casesextra]`: stuck-**open** EGR requires NOₓ ≈ 0 — a high NOₓ at 2500 RPM rules out stuck-open and points here (stuck-closed / restricted). **Consumer:** dual-idle delta routing (→ TEST_RPM_SEPARATION_MATRIX, GASWIKI-08). Source: `casesextra` Case 2.
- **discriminator:** GASLab confirms how the timing error affects combustion. Solenoid faults post P0011–P0014 — DTCLab's job.

- **phaser-lag dual-idle signature** `[v2.2: casesextra]`: a sluggish/mechanically-retarded phaser (worn phaser, low oil pressure, OCV-passage sludge) holds the cam at max retard **at idle** → poor scavenging, partial burn: HC **400 ppm**, CO₂ **12.2 %**, O₂ **1.1 %**, λ **1.04** at idle. At 2500 RPM oil pressure rises, the phaser reaches commanded angle and scavenging normalises: HC **→ 50 ppm (Δ ≈ −350 ppm)**, CO₂ **→ 14.0 %**, O₂ **→ 0.3 %**, λ **→ 1.005**. The **HC reversal on rev-up is the defining signature — a misfire does not clear this way**. DTC context P0011 / P0021. **Consumer:** dual-idle delta routing (→ TEST_RPM_SEPARATION_MATRIX, GASWIKI-08). Source: `casesextra` Case 3.

- **discriminator:** saturated canister delivers continuous unmetered vapour; ECU pushes negative trims but cannot fully compensate. Manifests at mid-load (post tip-in), not idle. DTCs P0441–P0458 may or may not be set.

- **purge-valve-stuck-open dual-idle signature** `[v2.2: casesextra]`: at idle the purge solenoid is commanded closed, so gas reads clean; on rev-up the ECU raises purge duty and a stuck-open valve dumps canister vapour uncontrolled. Result is **rich specifically on rev-up**: λ **1.00 → 0.92 (Δλ ≈ −0.08)**, HC **40 → 250 ppm**, CO **0.12 → 2.0 %** from idle to 2500 RPM; DTC context P0441 + P0172. The **idle-clean→2500-rich delta is the differentiator** from → FAULT_VACUUM_REGULATOR_DIAPHRAGM_RUPTURE (rich *at idle*, **improves** on rev as vacuum drops) and from a steady fuelling-rich (flat across RPM). **Consumer:** dual-idle delta routing (→ TEST_RPM_SEPARATION_MATRIX, GASWIKI-08). Source: `casesextra` Case 1.

- **chemical_state:** `EGR_DILUTION_MISFIRE` · **dna_gate:** `requires_dtc: true` (ontology-level gate, not a `dna_gate`; `resolution.py` does not consume `requires_dtc` in v1) · **match_class:** SPECIFIC
- **gas_vector:** HC moderate (200–400) | CO low–moderate (elevated) | CO₂ **low (< 11.5 %)** | O₂ **high (> 2 %, false lean)** | NOₓ **very low (< 30 ppm, quenched)** | λ **> 1.05 (false lean)**

- **discriminator:** coolant entering the chamber quenches the flame, suppresses NOₓ, displaces CO₂ with steam, and produces white sweet-smelling exhaust. May present as `SAMPLE_INVALID` if water condenses in the sample line. **Signature persists at 2500 RPM** and crucially **NOₓ fails to rise** with revs (a healthy engine spikes NOₓ at 2500 RPM) — the endothermic vaporisation of entering water keeps temps below the thermal-NOₓ threshold. Confirm with cooling-system pressure test + combustion leak detector.

- **head-gasket oil-to-cylinder breach sub-mode** `[v2: q4]`: a head-gasket failure between a pressurised **oil** passage and the bore (often alongside a coolant passage) presents with the same false-lean + suppressed-NOₓ fingerprint (HC 340, CO 0.65, O₂ 2.6, NOₓ 18, λ 1.085 at idle; HC 440, O₂ 2.1, NOₓ 38, λ 1.055 at 2500). It routes to `COOLANT_LEAK_INTERNAL` for v2 emit; candidate value `HEAD_GASKET_OIL_BREACH` is recorded in → CONCEPT_PROPOSED_ENUM_ADDITIONS (GASWIKI-11). Tell-tale beyond gases: milky oil/coolant emulsion on the dipstick.

# 7. Catalyst & Post-Cat Logic
> **Chunk summary.** TWC chemistry and the diagnostics that depend on it, ending with the v2 dual-idle catalyst test that distinguishes a recoverable weak converter from a dead one.
## 7.1 How a three-way cat works {#CONCEPT_TWC}
Oxidation:  2 CO + O₂  →  2 CO₂
Reduction:  2 NO + 2 CO →  N₂ + 2 CO₂
## 7.2 Pre- vs post-cat efficiency {#CONCEPT_PRE_POST_CAT_EFFICIENCY}
| Healthy engine + healthy cat | ~95 % | > 99 % | 0.1 – 0.45 % | < 35 ppm | < 0.35 % |
| Rich mixture + healthy cat | < 90 % | ~ 90 % | High (> 1 %) | Moderate | Very low |
| Misfire + healthy cat | < 80 % | < 85 % | Moderate | Very high | High |
**CO-drop expectations:** no air pump — max CO drop ≈ 2 % across a working cat (1.0 → ~0.05 %); with air pump — up to 8 % drop (8 → 0.1 %).
## 7.3 Post-cat O₂ sensor diagnostic {#CONCEPT_POSTCAT_O2_DIAGNOSTIC}

The downstream O₂ sensor is a switching narrowband for OBD-II monitoring. With a healthy cat the rear sensor is slow and flat (oxygen storage absorbs ECU oscillations). When the cat degrades it begins to mirror the upstream — high-frequency switching at cross-counts approaching 1:1 is the OBD test for P0420/P0430. GASLab does not consume the switching directly (OBDLab's job), but COMLab can pass `downstream_o2_sensor_switching` so GASLab can raise `rule_downstream_mirroring_upstream` if the chemistry agrees.

**The false-P0420 trap (gas refutes the DTC) `[v2.2: casesextra]`.** A failed *downstream* O₂ sensor that mimics upstream switching sets P0420 on a **perfectly healthy catalyst**. The gas analyser breaks the tie: a truly failed cat produces breakthrough gases (tailpipe **HC > 80 ppm, CO > 0.2 %, and/or elevated O₂**), whereas pristine tailpipe chemistry — **CO < 0.05 %, HC < 25 ppm, CO₂ > 14.5 %, λ 0.98–1.02 at both idle and 2500 RPM** — with P0420 set is a **downstream-sensor fault until proven otherwise**, not a cat. **Routing:** `P0420 present AND tailpipe chemistry clean at both speeds` ⇒ suppress `CATALYST_OVERWHELMED`/`CATALYST_NOT_LIGHTING_OFF` and surface the downstream-O₂-sensor candidate (OBDLab confirms via the rear-sensor waveform). **Consumer:** catalyst-vs-sensor disambiguation in COMLab fault-atlas routing — prevents an expensive catalyst misdiagnosis. Source: `casesextra` Case 7.
## 7.4 NOₓ capacity and the CO-to-NOₓ transition {#CONCEPT_NOX_CAPACITY}

The reduction bed can process ≈ **2000 ppm NOₓ** under normal conditions; NOₓ above this cannot be addressed by the converter alone — focus on EGR, timing, combustion temperature, not converter replacement.
## 7.5 Converter rejuvenation — controlled misfire {#TEST_REJUVENATION}

Converters coated with carbon/sulfur (not physically destroyed) can be revived by controlled heating: confirm structurally intact → induce a controlled misfire to push extra HC to the cat → HC oxidises on the surface, raising temperature → burns off the coating. **Never let shell temperature exceed 800 °F (427 °C).** Last resort, not routine.
## 7.6 The dual-idle catalyst efficiency test {#TEST_DUAL_IDLE_CATALYST}

`[v2: q10]` An on-site method for 1990–2010 petrol that isolates whether an emissions failure is a dead converter, a weak/degraded converter, or engine-out fuel control — using a **low-idle + 2500 RPM 5-gas and λ** comparison.

**Step 1 — precondition (validate fuel control first).** A cat cannot process bad feed gas. Check tailpipe λ at both speeds: it must hold tightly in **0.995–1.005** (or at least 0.98–1.02 to light off). Because λ is combustion-invariant (→ CONCEPT_BRETTSCHNEIDER), if λ sits in window but pollutants are high, fuel management is healthy and the failure is purely catalytic.
**Step 2 — the idle ↔ 2500 RPM delta:**
| Case | At 2500 RPM (hot, high flow) | At low idle (cooled) | Verdict |

| **Weak / degraded** (thermal "go-out") | CO₂ 14.5–16 %, O₂ < 0.5 %, CO < 0.2 %, HC < 35 ppm | **distinct divergence**: CO₂ 13.5–14.5 %, O₂ 0.3–0.7 %, CO 0.5–0.9 %, HC 75–125 ppm — despite λ ≈ 1.000 | Weak/lazy/partially contaminated cat (lost active surface area, "goes out" when cooled) |
| **Dead / melted / poisoned** | raw engine-out: CO₂ < 13.5 %, HC > 100, CO > 0.5 %, O₂ > 0.5 % | identical raw readings — **no delta** | Catastrophic loss of all oxygen-storage/conversion |

**Step 3 — confirming chemical markers:** (1) **CO₂ maximisation** — healthy CO₂ is 1–2 % higher at 2500 RPM than idle, peaking ~15–16 %; healthy engine but CO₂ < 14 % at 2500 ⇒ cat failing to oxidise carbon. (2) **O₂/CO balance** — both > 0.5 % simultaneously while λ is perfect ⇒ reactants present but the cat is inactive and failing to combine them.

**Routing.** A clear idle-vs-2500 delta with λ in window ⇒ `CATALYST_NOT_LIGHTING_OFF` (recoverable, → FAULT_CATALYST_NOT_LIGHTING_OFF); raw readings at both speeds with engine-out pollution beyond cat capacity ⇒ `CATALYST_OVERWHELMED` (→ FAULT_CATALYST_OVERWHELMED). This test is the catalyst arm of → TEST_RPM_SEPARATION_MATRIX (GASWIKI-08).
## 7.7 Catalyst & O₂-sensor poisoning agents {#CONCEPT_CATALYST_POISONING_AGENTS}

`[v2.2: cases_petrol]` Poisoning is chemically distinct from thermal failure: a poisoned cat is coated/adsorbed (often recoverable for sulphur, never for lead), a thermally-failed cat is melted/collapsed. **History splits them:** oil-burn / coolant-leak / leaded-fuel ⇒ poisoning; prolonged misfire / very-rich / over-rev ⇒ thermal. The four field agents, their source, tailpipe/sensor signature, reversibility, and the DNA gate COMLab uses to admit the agent-specific verdict:

| **Silicon (Si)** | RTV silicone sealant in intake/exhaust; coolant silicate inhibitors entering the chamber | Glassy SiO₂ on Pt/Pd sites. **O₂ sensor poisoned first** — white/beige glassy deposit on the sensor tip, then HC creeps up and efficiency falls over weeks | **No** (mechanical coating) | `contamination_history.silicone` OR coolant-loss co-signature; pairs with → FAULT_O2_SENSOR_BIASED_LOW (GASWIKI-05) |

| **Phosphorus / Zinc (P/Zn, ZDDP)** | ZDDP anti-wear additive in engine oil, entering when oil burns (rings / valve seals) | Oil-burn signature (**HC high, fuel trims ≈ 0 %**) **plus** progressive efficiency decline. Commonest long-term poison on high-mileage engines | **No** (gradual, months) | **Always gated on an oil-burn co-signature** (→ FAULT_WORN_VALVE_SEALS / FAULT_WORN_PISTON_RINGS / FAULT_POA_SIGNATURE). Fix the oil burn first or the new cat re-poisons |

| **Sulphur (S)** | High-sulphur fuel | Temporary efficiency loss; **rotten-egg H₂S smell** (a healthy cat converts H₂S → odourless SO₂; a poisoned bed lets H₂S pass). **Intermittent P0420 after high-S fuelling that clears after a desulph event** | **Partial** — desulphurises on sustained high-load (cat > ~600 °C) | `fuel_quality.high_sulphur`; intermittent-P0420-with-no-mechanical-cause prior |
## 7.8 Healthy-catalyst masking (the "filter of truth" limit) {#CONCEPT_HEALTHY_CAT_MASKING}

`[v2.3: EP-CAT-02, EP-CAT-05; Vol1 N-008]` This is the inverse of a catalyst-failure diagnosis: the catalyst is healthy, lit, and high-OSC, so it scrubs the evidence of a sick engine before the tailpipe probe can see it. A leaking injector, high fuel pressure, GDI HPFP leak, or oil-burn feed can arrive at the cat as rich / HC-heavy gas; the converter oxidises CO + HC, buffers O₂ swings, and the **tailpipe** may still show near-normal HC/CO/O₂ with λ inside the catalyst window (0.97–1.03). The cat is doing its job; that is exactly why it hides the engine.

- The dual-idle / RPM behaviour (→ TEST_DUAL_IDLE_CATALYST §7.6; → TEST_RPM_SEPARATION_MATRIX in GASWIKI-08) can still expose a *cat* fault. A healthy cat masking a rich engine may show no useful gas delta, which is the trap.

**What tailpipe gas cannot do.** Tailpipe 5-gas alone cannot confirm or exonerate the engine upstream of a healthy catalyst. A clean downstream sample means the post-cat chemistry is clean; it does **not** prove the engine-out feed gas was healthy. This concept only applies when a catalyst is present / known, consistent with the `has_catalyst` scope shrinkage in GASWIKI-10 §10.2.

- **Pre-cat (upstream) O₂ stuck rich (> ~0.7 V) + negative LTFT at idle and cruise, while tailpipe λ remains in-window** ⇒ masked rich engine (EP-CAT-02). Pre-cat O₂ and LTFT are OBDLab perception channels and COMLab fusion evidence, not GASLab analyser inputs.
- **Pre-cat inference from catalyst inlet/outlet ΔT** (EP-CAT-05) ⇒ infer the feed-gas chemistry from the heat the cat releases; this is a COMLab L5 step, not a GASLab verdict.
**Urgency.** Masked rich can drive the catalyst substrate toward thermal damage (~1000 °C, Denton §5). Flag and route it; do not clear it as a healthy engine.

# 8. Diagnostic Tactics
> **Chunk summary.** The pre-test conditions and the bench tactics GASLab reasoning assumes, including the v2 RPM-differential family-separation matrix and the probe-occlusion sampling-leak test.
## 8.1 Pre-test conditions {#TEST_PRECONDITIONS}
| Engine warm (ECT > 60 °C / past light-off) | Operating envelope; cold samples out of scope |
| 5-gas analyser confirmed (NOₓ channel live) | Operating envelope; no 4-gas fallback |
| Vehicle stabilised at idle ≥ 60 s | OBD trims need time to settle |
## 8.4 Lambda-mismatch test (sensor fraud) {#TEST_LAMBDA_MISMATCH}
## 8.5 The "weird gases" decision tree {#TEST_WEIRD_GASES_TREE}
| CO high + O₂ high | Triangle | Sum > 16 % → ingress; normal → rich misfire |
| HC > 2000 ppm | Cylinder contribution | Likely mechanical / oil |
| Triangle sum > 18 % | Probe not in pipe / engine off | Refuse to diagnose |
## 8.9 The idle→2500 RPM family-separation matrix {#TEST_RPM_SEPARATION_MATRIX}

`[v2: q7, q4]` The single most powerful on-site tactic for separating the candidate families is to watch how the five gases and λ move from low idle (~750 RPM) to high idle (2500 RPM). The defining question for each family is **does the signature normalise, persist, or worsen with RPM?**
| Family | Low idle | At 2500 RPM | Separating mechanism |

| **Lean (vacuum/fuel)** | O₂ > 3 %, CO < 0.1 %, HC 150–400, λ > 1.15 | O₂ < 1 %, CO₂ 14–15 %, HC < 50, λ → 1.0 | A fixed vacuum leak becomes insignificant against metered air at 2500 → **normalises** |
| **Catalyst (failing)** | CO₂ > 12 %, CO 0.5–1.5 %, HC 100–300, λ 0.995–1.005 | same | λ stays perfectly stoich; high CO₂ proves in-cylinder combustion is fine → cat-only fault |
| **Sensor (biased O₂/MAF)** | rich bias: CO > 3 %, O₂ < 0.2 %, λ < 0.85 | CO stays > 3 %, λ < 0.85 | Sensor offsets are flat/continuous → **do not normalise** with RPM |
| **Misfire (electrical)** | HC > 1000, O₂ > 3 %, CO < 0.2 %, CO₂ < 10 % | persists | Raw air+fuel in strict ratio; CO stays low (no combustion in that cylinder) |
| **ECU timing (adv/ret)** | advanced: HC 120–250, CO < 0.2 %, NOₓ ~ 0 | advanced: NOₓ > 1200, λ ~ 1.0, MAP normal | Vacuum stays healthy; λ held at 1.0 by closed loop → no trim corrections |

| **Mechanical (valve/rings)** | burnt valve: HC > 500, O₂ > 2 %, CO₂ < 11 % | burnt valve: HC drops > 50 %, CO₂ rises | Localised fixed leak masked by velocity at speed; jumped cam affects all cylinders continuously |

**Oil-burn sub-cut** (once misfire is ruled out by HC magnitude): **HC drops sharply** at 2500 ⇒ worn valve seals; **HC + CO rise** at 2500 ⇒ worn piston rings; **HC flat, moderate** ⇒ generally worn engine; **HC extreme but λ perfectly stoich, CO ≈ 0** ⇒ turbo turbine-seal oil leak; **NOₓ fails to rise** with high O₂ ⇒ internal coolant/head-gasket leak. See → CONCEPT_RPM_DIFFERENTIAL_DISCRIMINATOR (GASWIKI-06A).

> Deeper OBD-II isolation for timing faults — DTC correlation (P0016–P0019), Mode `$06` MID/TID, freeze-frame, and in-cylinder pressure waveform (EVO/IVO/IVC phasing) — sits outside GASLab's tailpipe-only emit boundary and is owned by **OBDLab / DTCLab**. GASLab consumes their verdicts as corroboration, not as inputs to `chemical_state`.
## 8.10 The probe-occlusion test (sampling-leak isolation) {#TEST_PROBE_OCCLUSION}

`[v2: q3]` When the analyser shows high O₂ / false-lean λ but the engine runs smoothly and OBD STFT is ≈ 0, suspect a leak in the sampling apparatus rather than the exhaust. **Procedure:** block the probe tip (e.g. with a finger). On an intact system the vacuum pump should stall and the O₂ reading should drop to near 0 %. If O₂ does **not** drop, there is a physical leak in the sampling hose/fittings — the "lean" is an artefact. Pair with the STFT correlation in → CONCEPT_LEAK_VS_SAMPLING before emitting `EXHAUST_AIR_LEAK`.
**TEST_PRECONDITIONS** GATED_BY **warm engine, closed-loop, 60 s stabilised idle**
**TEST_LAMBDA_MISMATCH** DETECTS **truth-vs-perception divergence** — Δλ > 0.08 triggers override
**TEST_LAMBDA_MISMATCH** ROUTES_TO **RULE_LAMBDA_MISMATCH** (GASWIKI-04)
**TEST_RPM_SEPARATION_MATRIX** DISAMBIGUATED_BY **idle vs 2500 RPM gas delta** — separates ignition vs cam timing, weak vs dead cat, oil-burn leaf faults
**TEST_PROBE_OCCLUSION** VERIFIES **sample-stream integrity** — blocks probe tip, O₂ must drop to near 0 %
**FAULT_IGNITION_MISFIRE** CONSUMES **GasLabDnaView.cylinder_count** via `inferred_misfiring_cylinder_count ≈ O₂ / (21 / N)`
- **TEST_PRECONDITIONS** — warm engine, closed-loop, 60 s stabilised idle. Gates all gas interpretation. Consumer: `rule_engine.classify` entry guard.
- **TEST_LAMBDA_MISMATCH** — chemistry λ (Brettschneider) vs ECU λ comparison; Δλ thresholds: ≤0.05 proceed, 0.05–0.08 borderline, >0.08 override. Consumer: `RULE_LAMBDA_MISMATCH`.

# 10. Limited-Scope Behaviour & Confidence Ceilings
User decision (2026-05-19): "vehicle without clear DNA profile — there will be limited diagnostic scope in order not to break the diagnostic engine."
## 10.1 Confidence levels {#CONCEPT_CONFIDENCE_LEVEL}
## 10.2 Scope shrinkage {#CONCEPT_SCOPE_SHRINKAGE}

| Chemistry-pure: `NORMAL_OPERATION`, `RICH_MIXTURE`, `LEAN_MIXTURE`, `IGNITION_MISFIRE`*, `LEAN_MISFIRE`, `RICH_MISFIRE`, `EXHAUST_AIR_LEAK`, `HIGH_COMBUSTION_TEMP`, `SAMPLE_INVALID`, `TIMING_OVER_ADVANCED`, `TIMING_RETARDED`, `O2_SENSOR_BIASED_LOW/HIGH`, `WORN_ENGINE`, `FLAT_CAMSHAFT`, `VACUUM_REGULATOR_DIAPHRAGM_RUPTURE`, `WORN_VALVE_SEALS`, `WORN_PISTON_RINGS`, `POA_SIGNATURE`, `CAM_TIMING_RETARDED_MAP`, `CAM_TIMING_RETARDED_MAF`, `CAM_TIMING_ADVANCED`, `VVT_FAILURE`, `EVAP_CANISTER_SATURATED`, `INCOMPLETE_OXIDATION`, `INCOMPLETE_COMBUSTION`, `COOLANT_LEAK_INTERNAL` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
## 10.3 Threshold widening {#CONCEPT_THRESHOLD_WIDENING}

When `target_lambda_v112` / `co_low_idle` / `co_high_idle` are absent, GASLab uses per-era defaults (→ CONCEPT_EURO_SCALING) instead of per-vehicle CoC bounds. Recommended widening: **±30 % at PARTIAL, ±50 % at NONE** on each numeric threshold, to avoid brittle pass/fail boundaries without a vehicle-specific reference.
## 10.4 What COMLab sees

`GasLabPayload.chemical_state` is always one of the 34 enum values. Limited scope is reflected as a smaller candidate set at the engine layer; COMLab sees the chosen value and a confidence note in the warnings stream. There is no separate `LIMITED_SCOPE` enum value.

Known confidence limit: when `has_catalyst` is true / known, a clean tailpipe downstream of a healthy catalyst cannot exonerate the engine on gas alone. The healthy-cat masking trap routes to → CONCEPT_HEALTHY_CAT_MASKING (GASWIKI-07 §7.8) and needs OBDLab/COMLab evidence to resolve.
## 10.5 Confidence ceiling for the top-3 emission {#CONCEPT_CONFIDENCE_CEILING}

Licenses the numeric confidence bounds GASLab uses when it emits a ranked **top-3** `(family, confidence)` list (the statistical-architecture exit). It is the gas-chemistry grounding for those literals.

**Principle.** A reading's diagnostic confidence is bounded by two things GASLab actually has: (a) **how specifically the chemistry pinned the verdict** — a multi-channel named override (→ RULE_MASKING…RULE_LAMBDA_MISMATCH) or a narrow single-fault band is more certain than a deliberately broad catch-all (`POA_SIGNATURE`, `VVT_FAILURE`) or a no-match fallback; and (b) **how tight the reference bounds were** — the DNA-confidence tier, because `HIGH` applies per-vehicle CoC bounds while `PARTIAL`/`NONE` widen them ±30 %/±50 %. Confidence is therefore a **ceiling = f(match type × DNA tier)** — never a function of the family. There is no per-family constant to inflate (deliberate: it forecloses per-family literal-tuning).
| `SPECIFIC` | one non-catch-all fault won 5-gas + λ bound matching and survived differentiator resolution |

**Ceiling table.** The `HIGH` column holds the four anchors; `PARTIAL`/`NONE` are *derived* — the `HIGH` value ÷ the §10.3 widening factor (`PARTIAL` ÷ 1.30, `NONE` ÷ 1.50). The only free parameters are the four `HIGH` anchors.
| Match type | `HIGH` (anchor) | `PARTIAL` (÷1.30) | `NONE` (÷1.50) |

**Why the anchors sit there.** `1.00` is reserved — GASLab reads one evidence channel and must not claim certainty alone (cross-lab corroboration is COMLab's job). `DEFINITIVE` 0.90 reflects multi-gas agreement (e.g. masking: HC ≫ 1000 **and** O₂ > 3 % **and** NOₓ < 50). `SPECIFIC` 0.80 is a single narrow-band match. `CATCH_ALL` 0.55 mirrors "ranked last". `FALLBACK` 0.50 is honest uncertainty (absence of a match is weak evidence of health).

**Application.** The per-candidate raw score (signature specificity + count of corroborating channels) is **clamped** to the ceiling for its `(match type, DNA tier)`: emitted confidence = `min(raw_score, ceiling)` ∈ [0,1]. Each candidate is scored/clamped on its own match type. GASLab emits per-candidate confidences and **does not normalise them to sum to 1** — ensemble normalisation across labs is COMLab's Bayesian fusion step.
**CONCEPT_SCOPE_SHRINKAGE** GATED_BY **CONCEPT_DNA_GATED_INGESTION** (GASWIKI-01) — no per-vehicle bounds, no HIGH lane
**CONCEPT_THRESHOLD_WIDENING** DERIVED_FROM **HIGH anchor ÷ widening factor** — PARTIAL ÷ 1.30, NONE ÷ 1.50
**CONCEPT_CONFIDENCE_CEILING** STATES **DEFINITIVE 0.90, SPECIFIC 0.80, CATCH_ALL 0.55, FALLBACK 0.50** (HIGH anchors)
**CONCEPT_CONFIDENCE_CEILING** CONSUMED_BY **COMLab Bayesian fusion** — GASLab emits per-candidate confidences, never normalises to sum=1
**match_class** GATED_BY **CONCEPT_CONFIDENCE_CEILING** — FALLBACK → 0.50, SPECIFIC → 0.80, DEFINITIVE → 0.90, CATCH_ALL → 0.55
- **CONCEPT_CONFIDENCE_LEVEL** — HIGH (per-vehicle CoC bounds), PARTIAL (÷1.30 widening), NONE (÷1.50 widening). Consumer: `GasLabDnaView.confidence` → `rule_engine._coc_adjust_normal_bounds`.
- **CONCEPT_THRESHOLD_WIDENING** — PARTIAL ÷1.30, NONE ÷1.50 from HIGH anchors. Consumer: `rule_engine._coc_adjust_normal_bounds`.
- **CONCEPT_CONFIDENCE_CEILING** — ceiling = f(match_type × DNA tier): anchors 0.90/0.80/0.55/0.50. Consumer: `rule_engine._definitive_match` → COMLab fusion.

- **Light-off** — Catalyst surface reaching self-sustaining reaction temperature (~400 °C).
- **Modified Brettschneider** — HC carbon-mass-corrected form (factor 12 vs 6); noted for future calibration.

## 6. Lambda from chemistry — formal definition
[CO₂] + [CO]/2 + [O₂]
HC_FACTOR = 0.0025   (ppm HC → effective vol % in the carbon balance)
λ_5gas = λ₄ + (NOₓ_ppm / 1e6) × 0.5 / volumetric_sum_fraction
T-GASA-11 — `([CO₂] + [CO]/2 + [O₂] + (Hcv/4 · [CO₂]/([CO₂]+[CO])) · [CO₂]) / ([CO₂] + [CO] + [HC])` — is **not** a
definition: it has no `(1 + Hcv/4 …)` denominator normalisation and gives λ ≈ 1.45 for a stoichiometric sample
(F-C2-14). Adopting the full Brettschneider equation (with `Hcv` and the normalised denominator) would move every
verdict; it is a deferred design row (T-GASA-F14).
| `Hcv` | 1.85 | Hydrogen-to-carbon atomic ratio for pump petrol; not used by λ₄ (reserved for T-GASA-F14) |
| `AFR_stoich` | 14.71 | Stoichiometric petrol AFR (kg air / kg fuel) |
NOₓ adds a small O₂-equivalence term (~0.05 % per 1 000 ppm); on a 5-gas analyser it is included directly via the standard Brettschneider modification:
λ_5gas = λ_4gas  +  (NOₓ_ppm / 1e6) × 0.5 / volumetric_sum_fraction
### 6.1 Edge cases
| All gases ≈ 0 | `lambda_chem` returns the 1.0 sentinel; `classify()` flags `SAMPLE_INVALID` independently (T-AUD-16) |
| O₂ near 20.9 %, others ≈ 0 | λ → ∞; triangle gate catches this earlier |
| 4-gas reading (NOₓ missing) | **Reject** — operating envelope requires 5-gas |
### 6.2 Reliability and uncertainty band (v2)

`λ_chem` is an exhaust-gas **mass balance** — a property of the *sample*, not a direct measure of in-cylinder combustion. Reliability is governed by sample-stream integrity, not the formula. Source: wiki §2.4 (GASWIKI-02); research q1, q2.
| Headline equation accuracy (clean inputs) | ~ ± 1 % | de-facto industry standard |
| Calibrated analyser repeatability | ± 0.05 – 0.10 absolute λ | a drifted O₂ cell breaks the calc |
| Exhaust/sampling air leak swing | 0.05 – 0.15 (5–15 % false-lean) | the "ground-truth killer"; resolve via STFT + probe-occlusion |
| Misfire | λ stays ≈ 1.0 (misfire-immune) | read HC/O₂, not λ |
`modified_brettschneider` (HC carbon factor 12 vs 6) is **noted but not adopted** — current `hc_equiv = hc * 0.0025` NDIR scaling is the v2 production method.

## 13. Invariants the GASLab code must enforce
1. **Five inputs always.** No 4-gas fallback path. Missing NOₓ → reject upstream.
2. **Triangle first.** No `chemical_state` other than `SAMPLE_INVALID` may be emitted unless `sample_validity` is `VALID`, `BORDERLINE`, or `EXTERNAL_O2_SUSPECT`.
3. **Single chemical state.** GASLab returns exactly one `chemical_state`; ambiguity is collapsed by rule priority (the rule engine has named overrides — see wiki §8.4–§8.6).

4. **Output never exceeds Pydantic bounds.** The values in `GasLabPayload` are pre-validated against §12.1 ranges before emission. If the rule engine would produce out-of-bound values, that is a code bug.
5. **DNA gates are honoured.** A `ChemicalSignature` value with a DNA gate in §3.1 cannot be emitted unless the gate evaluates to `true` against the current `GasLabDnaView`.

6. **No COMLab imports.** GASLab declares its own enums (this file is the spec). COMLab independently mirrors them in `comlab/schemas/vocabulary.py`. Two independent declarations of the same StrEnum are intentional — JSON values are the cross-lab contract, not Python classes.

7. **Confidence does not shrink the candidate set (T-AUD-16).** The DNA gate applies strictly at every confidence. On the `process()` path `confidence` is read only for the `co_high_idle` override; the wiki §10 candidate-set restriction for `PARTIAL`/`NONE` is not applied.
